parts.note: an evicted tenant is thrown out with every case and holdall they own, everything they have

explanation.surface: A housing lawyer's file of eviction cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like legal cases; read it as luggage, and the phrase for being thrown out with all your belongings appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Being turned out with all one's possessions is the idiom for a complete, total eviction.

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is still offered yet another kind of banger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb; it is the verb meaning to calm. 'a variety of' rearranges SAUSAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To still pain or fear is to soothe or calm it.

definitions.meaning: a unit of land measure, 4,840 square yards
a port city on the coast of northern Israel

explanation.surface: A question about the size of a piece of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an imperial unit of land area and a historic port city in Israel.

clue.text: Possibly end with a true version, though it's altogether false

indicators.note: possibly signals that the words may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A debate about whether ending with a true version makes a story honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' and 'version' both point to rearranging END and TRUE; 'with a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A full set of false teeth is wholly artificial.

clue.text: Caused trouble, getting Bill and Edward out of bed

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
Ted is a short form of Edward
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Two people named Bill and Edward are roused and misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving badly or misbehaving, as a child might, is the idiom for making trouble.

indicators.note: doing something wildly suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Revellers who have had too much sing wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're drunk' looks like a description of the singers; it defines spirits that are drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: These are spirits that people drink, plural to match 'they're'.

clue.text: Have fun on leave near Portsmouth

indicators.note: on means the piece is placed after the other one here

parts.note: to leave is to go
to sport is to play or have fun

explanation.surface: A sailor enjoys shore leave in the Portsmouth area.
explanation.walkthrough: GOSPORT is a naval town across the harbour from Portsmouth on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This town sits across the harbour from the naval city, a place in its neighbourhood.

clue.text: Sign up ace goal maker, an England player

indicators.note: a maker builds something new from material, so these letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: An England club urges the signing of a top goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maker' rearranges SIGN UP ACE GOAL. PAUL GASCOIGNE, 'Gazza', was an England footballer of the late 1980s and 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a celebrated footballer who won caps for the national side.

parts.note: mounted means launched, but also on horseback: an onslaught by soldiers on horses

explanation.surface: A military assault is launched.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge by horse soldiers is an offensive literally made on horseback.

parts.note: out of place reads as unplaced: a runner who finishes outside the first three

explanation.surface: A competitor who seems not to belong.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or contestant that fails to finish in the first places is an unplaced loser.

clue.text: A unit is ordered to somewhere in North Africa

indicators.note: the words are put in a new order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military unit receives orders to deploy to North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a military command; it rearranges A UNIT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a country on the Mediterranean coast between Algeria and Libya.

clue.text: Charge the boy nothing to go in

indicators.note: one piece goes in, meaning it is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone charges a boy nothing for admission.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a burden or quantity carried, as in a gun's charge.

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken, so it sounds like another

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or ridicule them

explanation.surface: A leader is mocked in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows the way and leads others is a leader.

clue.text: Hoax article used as a tail-piece

parts.note: cod as an adjective means sham or mock, a hoax
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A spoof article is used as a closing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In music it is a concluding passage tacked on at the end.

clue.text: Blame one put on the head of Dean Swift

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Blame is put on Dean Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean Swift' points to Jonathan Swift, dean of St Patrick's in Dublin; split it so only D is taken from Dean and Swift is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast and quick means swift.

parts.note: One character of that title is a competitor

explanation.surface: Someone who competed with the playwright Sheridan.
explanation.definitionFit: A single competitor, and one of the title figures of Sheridan's play The Rivals.

parts.note: to aver is to assert
age brings seniority

explanation.surface: Someone means to pull rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean is the arithmetic middle value of a set.

parts.note: pointing at people is rude; a gun dog that stands to indicate game does just that

explanation.surface: A badly behaved dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of gun dog named for its habit of indicating game, which is rude in people.

clue.text: A number keeping secret get a telling off

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
hiding means keeping secret

explanation.surface: Someone keeping a secret gets told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding is a reproof or rebuke.

parts.note: die read as a noun, a gaming cube, made of something frozen

explanation.surface: Someone perishes from cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A die is a cube; one of frozen water is what goes in drinks.

clue.text: Girl I sign on as an astronomer

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A girl signs up as an astronomer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian scientist who studied Jupiter's moons through a telescope was a stargazer.

definitions.meaning: illicit commerce, as in drug dealing
cars and lorries moving on roads

explanation.definitionFit: It means both dealing in goods and the flow of cars on a road.

clue.text: Strong blow wrenched a door half off

parts.note: torn means wrenched or ripped

indicators.note: with half taken off, only the first half of the word remains

explanation.surface: A strong gust wrenches a door half off its hinges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong blow' sounds like a punch; it is a violent wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent storm of wind.

definitions.meaning: a manner or style of doing things

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to form or create; as a noun, a manner or mode.

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone lowers a large cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like a verb of bringing down; it is lour, to scowl, rhyming with 'flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower (lour) is to scowl or frown, which is a fierce stare.

clue.text: Is taken back between a double land mass

indicators.note: between means the piece sits inside the other, flanked on each side
double asks for the preceding letter to be written twice, one copy after another
taken back means the word is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Something is taken back between two parties over territory.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest continent on Earth.

definitions.meaning: coarse sand spread on frozen roads

explanation.definitionFit: It means both pluck and the sand spread on roads in winter.

definitions.meaning: to have a go, as in having a try

explanation.surface: Someone tries to form a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a go or try and a lively celebration.

indicators.note: a new version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Selecting a gear in a new French car.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the gear position in which no drive is engaged.

clue.text: A parent with energy is extraordinary!

parts.note: ma is a mother, a parent
zing means energy or zest

explanation.surface: An energetic parent is remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishing and remarkable mean the same thing.

clue.text: An almost negligible amount, like one in ten

definitions.meaning: in the figure 10 the 1 stands beside the 0

explanation.definitionFit: It means a tiny quantity and, literally, beside zero, as the 1 is in 10.
